question: Does adding verified availability information change the model, and by how much?
design: Identical model, identical games, identical holdout. Only the personnel feature changes. This is the alternative to subtracting a fixed number of points for a missing starter, which no test in this repository supports.

with_personnel.empty_because: No absence in the corpus is confirmed. A depth-chart rank is not participation, and no inactive list, Game Book or snap count is captured (gates PG-ACTUAL-STARTER and PG-INACTIVE).

difference.would_be_readable_if: the paired 95% interval excluded zero; at this n the cluster SE of one arm is 0.0034, so a difference smaller than about 0.0094 Brier would be indistinguishable from noise

why_not_a_penalty: A fixed penalty encodes a belief about a player's value that has not been measured.
The measurement needs (a) a confirmed absence and (b) the same model run twice. (a) is missing.
Publishing the penalty anyway would make the model look informed while resting on an unmeasured assumption.
what_would_fill_the_arm: One season of official inactive lists joined to the corpus, so each game carries the set of confirmed absent starters. That is 136 inactive lists, of which 0 are captured.
